title: Suspected fracture
summary: Support in the position found, check circulation, and avoid unnecessary movement.
sources: 2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid — Fractures and Suspected Spinal Injury
WHO Basic Emergency Care: Approach to the Acutely Ill and Injured
actions: Do not move the person except for immediate safety, airway care, or CPR when a high-energy mechanism or spine injury is possible.
Support and immobilize the injured part in the position found. Keep joints above and below still when practical.
Check colour, warmth, and feeling beyond any splint before and after application. Loosen bindings if circulation worsens; do not straighten the limb.
Apply a cold pack wrapped in cloth without pressing on deformity or exposed bone.
Cover an open fracture with a dry sterile dressing without pushing bone back. Control bleeding by pressing around, not on, exposed bone.
prohibitions: Do not straighten or reduce a bone or joint.
Do not press on exposed bone or an embedded object.
Do not make the person walk on or test the injured part.

redFlags.text: Emergency warning signs selected—contact emergency services now.

emergencyCall.text: Call emergency services for an open fracture, loss of circulation or feeling, severe deformity, major mechanism, neck pain or possible spine, pelvis, or thigh injury.
